Stream predictions or diagnostics to a callback

Source: R/stream-methods.R
predict.fastglm_stream.Rd

Prediction for a large dataset can create a vector too large to retain in memory. A sink is a user-supplied function that receives one block of results at a time, for example to write predictions to a file or accumulate a summary. Without a sink, the result blocks are collected into a single R object, whose memory requirement grows with the number of observations.

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_stream'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("link", "response"),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  dispersion = NULL,
  sink = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a streaming GLM fit.

newdata

optional prediction data; otherwise rereads the fitted source.

type, dispersion, se.fit

prediction arguments as in [predict.fastglm()].

sink

optional function of `(value, chunk_index)` that processes or writes each result block. Its return value is ignored.

...

additional prediction arguments.

Value

Predictions (a `fastglm_prediction` list when `se.fit=TRUE`), or invisibly the number of chunks delivered to a sink. Each prediction block supplied to a sink uses the same structure. See fastglm-prediction-methods.
